::: {.why}
This is ascertainment bias with a ticker attached: you already know exactly why conditioning on survival distorts an estimate, so the only new content is how large the distortion is here.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Quantify, roughly, what backfilling today's index membership does to a backtested return, and say which direction it biases it.
- Name three distinct selection problems in a US equity universe and say which of them your free data source cannot fix.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Measure it on what you have: build an equal-weighted portfolio of today's S&P 500 members over 2010-today from your data, and compare its return to SPY's over the same window. The gap is not all survivorship, but it is mostly survivorship plus the weighting scheme, and separating the two is the exercise.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Write the three selection problems into reports/milestone-01-market-map.md: survivorship of delisted names, backfilled membership of index constituents, and the vendor's own coverage decision about what counts as a listed security. For each, name the fix and say whether you have access to it.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Check whether UW-Madison's WRDS subscription covers you. If it does, CRSP solves the first two of those three problems and the rest of the year gets materially better.
:::
:::
